records.excerpt: Title: SpaceX Stock Tumbles to Fresh Post-IPO Low Despite Imminent Flight Test Clearance URL Source: http://www.tikr.com/ja/blog/spacex-spcx-stock-plunge-all-time-low Published Time: 2026-07-14T12:30:00 Markdown Content: ## SpaceX**株の主要統計** * **SpaceX株の過去5日間の価格変動:** -12% * **7月13日時点の$SPCX株価:** $139 * **52週高値:** $226 * **$SPCX株価目標:**$242 _**\_****\\_[新機能公開: TIKRの新バリュエーションモデルで、お気に入りの銘柄の潜在的上昇余地を発見しよう（無料）](https://app.tikr.com/register?ref=tikrblog)\\_****\_**_**_[>>>](https://app.tikr.com/register?ref=tikrblog)_** ## 何が起きたのか？ SpaceX ([SPCX](https://app.tikr.com/stock/about?cid=7702894&tid=321424200&ref=49x9sy)) 株は月曜日に再び史上最安値を更新し、約4%下落して$140を割り込みました。これにより、[株価は同社の当初の$135というIPO価格に危険なほど近づいています](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c3wyj6e4210o)。わずか数週間前には$225まで取引されていた銘柄にとって、厳しい転換点です。 この下落は、良いニュースにもかかわらず起きました。[連邦航空局（FAA）が足止めしていた調査を終了](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/13/stocks-making-the-biggest-moves-midday-nio-brai-app-spcx-skhy.html)し、SpaceXが今週にも飛行試験を実施できるようになったのです。通常、この種の規制当局からのゴーサインは株価を押し上げるものです。しかし、SpaceX株は下落を続けました。 SpaceXは6月12日に上場し、投資家の大きな期待を集め、株価は$135の公募価格から初日終値$160.95まで上昇しました。翌週には株価が$225まで急騰し、一時的にSpaceXの時価総額がAmazonとMicrosoftを合わせた額を上回りました。 この初期の熱狂の多くはAIに関連していました。SpaceXがイーロン・マスクのAIスタートアップxAI（現在はSpaceXAI）を買収し、テック企業にデータセンター容量をリースし始めていたからです。 ![Image 1](https://res.cloudinary.com/tikr/images/w_3024,h_2016,c_scale/f_webp,q_auto/v1784026327/images/TIKR.com_SPCX-Space-Exploration-Technologies-Corp-2_1171920c188/TIKR.com_SPCX-Space-Exploration-Technologies-Corp-2_1171920c188.webp?_i=AA) SPCX株の売上高、EBIT、フリーキャッシュフロー予測（10億米ドル）（[TIKR](https://app.tikr.com/register?ref=tikrblog)） しかし、ロケットの建造・打ち上げとStarlink衛星ネットワークの運営というSpaceXのコア事業の現実が、株価に追いついてきているようです。 * Starlinkがテネシー州メンフィスで地元のデータセンター懸念の中、価格を引き下げた際、株価は1日で8%下落しました。 * SpaceXが7月7日にナスダック100種指数に採用された際、広範な指数が1.7%下落しただけなのに、同社は4.4%下落しました。 **[アナリストの成長予測とSpaceX株の株価目標を見る（無料） >>>](https://app.tikr.com/register?ref=tikrblog)** ## 市場がSpaceX株について伝えていること ウォール街は、SpaceX株がここからどこへ向かうかについて意見が分かれています。モルガン・スタンレーは$300の株価目標を設定しています。BofA証券は買いレーティングと$235の目標価格でカバレッジを開始したばかりです。 [BofAの強気のシナリオは、打ち上げコストの低下に大きく依存しています](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/as-spacex-stock-dips-near-ipo-price-bulls-like-bofas-epstein-say-buy-on-launch-leadership-150227637.html)。Falcon 9以前は1キログラムあたり約$10,000から$20,000だったコストが、Falcon 9では約$2,000に、そしてStarshipが完全に再利用可能になれば、1キログラムあたり$50から$100にまで下がる可能性があるとしています。 それでも、一部のアナリストは最近の上昇を、ファンダメンタルズよりも誇大広告に近いと見ています。 * CFRAのキース・スナイダー氏は、この株が「ミーム株のように見え始めた」と述べ、さらに下落して$115に向かうと予想しています。 * SpaceXの昨年の収益は180億ドルで、マスク氏が予測した2030年までの1兆ドルには遠く及ばない水準です。 ![Image 2](https://res.cloudinary.com/tikr/images/w_832,h_504,c_scale/f_webp,q_auto/v1784026371/images/SPCX-Street-Target-2_1171934e750/SPCX-Street-Target-2_1171934e750.webp?_i=AA) SPCX株のストリート・エスティメート（[TIKR](https://app.tikr.com/register?ref=tikrblog)） 次の本当の試練はすぐに訪れます。Starshipの飛行試験は7月16日に予定されていますが、BofAはその特定の飛行から大きな再利用性のマイルストーンが達成されるとは期待していません。 その後、すべての注目はSpaceXの最初の公開決算報告書（8月上旬に予定）に集まり、投資家はSpaceX株の現在の弱さが買い機なのか警告サインなのかをより明確に判断できるはずです。 **_**\_[](https://app.tikr.com/register?ref=tikrblog)**\\_[企業の公正価値を瞬時に推定（TIKRで無料） >>>](https://app.tikr.com/register?ref=tikrblog)\\_**\_**_** ## SpaceX株はここからどのくらい上昇余地があるのか？ TIKRの**新バリュエーションモデルツール**を使えば、1分以内に銘柄の潜在的な株価を推定できます。 必要なのは、3つのシンプルな入力だけです： 1. _売上高成長率_ 2. _営業マージン_ 3. _エグジットP/E倍率_ 何を入力すべきかわからない場合、TIKRはアナリストのコンセンサス予測を使用して各入力を自動的に入力し、迅速で信頼性の高い出発点を提供します。 そこから、TIKRは**強気、基本、弱気のシナリオ**の下での潜在的な株価と総リターンを計算し、銘柄が**割安か割高か**を素早く確認できるようにします。 [](https://app.tikr.com/register?ref=tikrblog)**_[**\_60秒以内に銘柄の真の価値を確認（TIKRで無料） >>>\_**](https://app.tikr.com/register?ref=tikrblog)_** ## 新しい機会を探していますか？ * **[億万長者投資家が何を買っているかを見る](https://app.tikr.com/register?ref=tikrblog)**ことで、賢い資金の動きを追うことができます。 * TIKRのオールインワンで使いやすいプラットフォームで、**[わずか5分で銘柄を分析](https://app.tikr.com/register?ref=tikrblog)**できます。 * より多くの石をひっくり返せば…より多くの機会が見つかります。**[TIKRで10万以上のグローバル銘柄、グローバルトップ投資家の保有銘柄などを検索。](https://app.tikr.com/register?ref=tikrblog)** ## **免責事項:** _TIKRの記事は、TIKRまたは当社のコンテンツチームからの投資または財務上のアドバイスとして提供されるものではなく、いかなる銘柄の売買を推奨するものでもないことにご注意ください。当社のコンテンツは、TIKRターミナルの投資データとアナリストの予測に基づいて作成されています。当社の分析には、最近の企業ニュースや重要なアップデートが含まれていない場合があります。TIKRは、記載されているいかなる銘柄にもポジションを保有していません。お読みいただきありがとうございます。幸運な投資を！_

records.title: SpaceX上場点火、イラン衝突が追い風に 米大手銀、4年半ぶり最強の投資銀行シーズンへ
records.excerpt: 米大手銀行が今週発表する第2四半期決算では、SpaceXの過去最大規模のIPO、大型M&Aの回復、イラン情勢を巡る地政学的緊張がもたらす市場変動を追い風に、上位5行の投資銀行手数料収入が111億ドル（約1.8兆円）と4年半ぶりの高水準に達する見通しだ。SpaceX案件だけで5億ドル（約810億円）の引受手数料が発生し、ゴールドマン・サックスとモルガン・スタンレーが各1億ドル（約160億円）を獲得した。銀行株は今年、市場全体をアウトパフォームし「安定の孤島」と目されている。アナリストは2027年までの利益モメンタム継続を予想する。市場の焦点は投資銀行・トレーディング部門の急成長に加え、純金利収入のガイダンスや個人向け与信の質にも向けられており、今回の決算は力強い成長の持続可能性を占う試金石となる。 米大手銀行が今週、米国株の決算シーズンの幕を切って落とす。市場の関心は投資銀行業務の爆発的な成長に集中している。SpaceXによる過去最大規模の新規株式公開（IPO）、大型M&A取引の回復、そしてイランを巡る地政学的衝突が引き起こす市場変動を追い風に、アナリストの間では金融機関が4年半ぶりとなる最も力強い投資銀行手数料収入を計上するとの見方が大勢だ。このモメンタムにより、銀行株は不安定な市場環境下で「安定の孤島」と見なされている。 JPモルガン・チェース（JPMorgan Chase, JPM）、バンク・オブ・アメリカ（Bank of America, BAC）、シティグループ（Citigroup, C）、ウェルズ・ファーゴ（Wells Fargo, WFC）、ゴールドマン・サックス（Goldman Sachs, GS）は、米東部時間火曜日の取引開始前に決算発表を予定しており、モルガン・スタンレー（Morgan Stanley, MS）は水曜日に発表する。これら金融大手6行の第2四半期純利益の合計は約440億ドル（約7.1兆円）と、前年同期比18%増加する見込みだ。 投資銀行業務が大爆発、SpaceXが強力な起爆剤に 今四半期決算の最大のハイライトは、間違いなく投資銀行業務である。市場予測データによると、米国の上位投資銀行5行の第2四半期における投資銀行手数料収入は前年同期比27%増の総額111億ドル（約1.8兆円）に達し、2021年の業界ピーク以来の高水準を記録する見通しだ。 この手数料急増の中心的な原動力となったのが、イーロン・マスク（Elon Musk）氏率いる宇宙開発企業SpaceXが6月に実施した過去最大のIPOだ。この上場案件だけで、23社の共同主幹事に総額5億ドル（約810億円）の引受手数料がもたらされた。これは世界史上最高額の上場引受手数料となる。このうち、ゴールドマン・サックスとモルガン・スタンレーは、それぞれ約1億ドル（約160億円）を獲得した。 ザックス・インベストメント・マネジメント（Zacks Investment Management）のチーフ市場ストラテジスト、ブライアン・マルベリー氏は「SpaceXの上場案件は規模が極めて大きく、引受に関与した全ての投資銀行が明確に恩恵を受けると予想している」と指摘する。直接的な引受手数料に加え、銀行はこの新規上場企業のための資金調達からも手数料を得ており、さらには新たに誕生したミリオネアやビリオネアの資産を運用する機会さえも獲得している。フロリダ大学（University of Florida）のファイナンス名誉教授ジェイ・リッター（Jay Ritter）氏はさらに、ゴールドマン・サックスとモルガン・スタンレーはSpaceXのIPOから、いわゆる「ソフトダラー」、すなわちヘッジファンドがIPOの超過割当枠を獲得するために投資銀行に支払う手数料も得ている可能性が高いと分析する。 株式資本市場業務だけではない。上位5行のM&A手数料収入も前年同期比約30%増加し、総額40億ドル（約6,500億円）を突破する見通しだ。これは2021年以来、同分野の手数料が3四半期連続で40億ドルの大台に乗る初めてのケースとなる。100億ドル（約1.6兆円）を超える大型M&A取引が明確に回復しており、モルガン・スタンレーは顧客向けリサーチレポートで、2026年の世界の公表済みM&A取引規模が過去最高を更新する可能性があると予測している。KBWのアナリスト、クリストファー・マクグラティ（Christopher McGratty）氏は、第2四半期の投資銀行業績は堅調で、株式引受が今四半期の焦点になるとの見方を示し、大型案件の価格決定に伴う高い発行量により、大手投資銀行が最も恩恵を受けると指摘した。 トレーディング業務は地政学的な追い風に乗る 投資銀行業務に加え、銀行のトレーディング部門も豊作の四半期を迎えた。イラン紛争などの地政学的な混乱が様々な資産クラスの変動性を高め、米金融機関のトレーダーに絶好の収益機会をもたらした。ウェルズ・ファーゴ（Wells Fargo）のシニアアナリスト、マイク・メイヨー（Mike Mayo）氏は、現在の金融業界は「スイートスポット」にあり、ウォール街とメインストリートという二大収益エンジンが稀に見る形で同時に成長モードに入っていると表現する。 メイヨー氏はCNBCの取材に対し、「史上最大のIPOを目の当たりにし、M&Aのペースは年間記録を更新する勢いであり、トレーディング活動は株式から債券、そして多くの地域へと拡大している」と述べた。KBWは、これら6行のトレーディング収入が前年同期比で14%急増する可能性があると予測している。マクグラティ氏は、銀行が変動性の上昇局面を捉える能力に秀でており、過去のサイクルで不意を突かれて打撃を受けた状況とは全く異なると指摘する。 銀行株は「安定の孤島」に、バリュエーションには依然妙味 人工知能（AI）による破壊的リスクやデジタル資産の採用に対する懸念が他セクターを揺るがす中、銀行株の今年に入ってからのパフォーマンスは堅調で、市場における「安定の孤島」と見なされている。KBWナスダック銀行指数は年初来で約14%上昇し、S&P500種指数の10%上昇をアウトパフォームしている。中でもモルガン・スタンレーとゴールドマン・サックスは年初来の上昇率が20%を超え、シティグループも同様に20%超の上昇、バンク・オブ・アメリカは約8.5%上昇している。唯一ウェルズ・ファーゴだけが年初来で株価が6.5%下落し、大手銀行の中での劣後銘柄となっている。 バンク・オブ・アメリカ・セキュリティーズ（BofA Securities）の北米銀行リサーチ責任者、エブラヒム・プーナワラ（Ebrahim Poonawala）氏は顧客向けレポートで、ロングオンリーの投資家やポートフォリオマネジャーは、2027年まで利益モメンタムが持続可能である証拠を求めていると指摘する。状況が継続すれば、投資家が半導体株の保有を減らす中で、銀行株は「信頼できる選択肢」となるという。同氏が選好する銀行株には、シティグループ、モルガン・スタンレー、ステート・ストリート（State Street, STT）、PNCファイナンシャル・サービシズ・グループ（PNC Financial Services, PNC）、ハンティントン・バンクシェアーズ（Huntington Bancshares, HBAN）、USバンコープ（U.S. Bancorp, USB）が含まれる。 銀行株の相対バリュエーション倍率は上昇したものの、KBWのアナリスト、マクグラティ氏は、その相対評価は依然として長期平均を大きく下回っていると強調する。KBWは総合銀行に対する強気の見方を維持しており、資本市場と資本還元における複数年にわたる構造的追い風の恩恵を受け続けるとの見解から、投資家にモルガン・スタンレーやPNCファイナンシャル・サービシズ・グループなどの株式をオーバーウエートとするよう推奨している。 純金利収入と経済見通しが焦点に 輝かしい投資銀行業務とトレーディングの陰で、銀行の本業である商業貸出と純金利収入にも転機が訪れようとしている。メイヨー氏は、商業貸出業務が長年の低迷を経て転換点を迎えた可能性があり、企業が不確実性を「新常態」として受け入れ、工場建設や投資計画を再開し始めていると見る。このトレンドは、フィフス・サード・バンコープ（Fifth Third Bancorp, FITB）などの地方銀行にとって特に有利に働く。 プーナワラ氏は、銀行の収益性の鍵は純金利収入の動向にあると指摘する。市場の焦点は、経営陣が資産の再価格設定、貸出成長、経営レバレッジを通じて預金獲得競争の圧力を相殺できるかどうかにある。同氏によれば、銀行が純金利収入の改善を実現できれば、投資家は緩やかな利ざや圧力をますます許容する姿勢を見せているという。市場全体が、米国で最大の資産規模を誇るJPモルガン・チェースが純金利収入のガイダンスを上方修正するかどうかに注目している。 金利見通しについては、KBWは米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）が今年利下げを行うとの予想を既に撤回し、年末のフェデラルファンド（FF）金利誘導目標は3.75%で据え置かれると予測、また10年物米国債利回りは2027年末までに4.4%に達すると予想している。市場では金利の「より高く、より長く」との見方がしっかりと定着している。 個人向け与信の質は全体として底堅さを維持しており、低失業率が貸出延滞率を低位に抑えている。しかし、HSBC（HSBC）の米国金融セクター株式リサーチ責任者、サウル・マルティネス（Saul Martinez）氏は、市場の期待ハードルは既に引き上げられており、株価の動きは楽観的な見通しをかなり織り込んでいると警告する。投資家は銀行のバランスシートを精査し、米国民の家計が圧迫されている兆候を探るだろう。 マルティネス氏は「本当に懸念すべきシナリオは、紛争が再び激化し、原油価格が大幅に反発、インフレが再燃する場合だ。そうなって初めて経済成長が憂慮されることになる」と分析する。2年連続で市場全体をアウトパフォームした後、市場が銀行株に投げかける問いは、「前四半期はどれほど強かったか」から、「この全ては持続可能なのか」へと移り変わっている。

records.title: デジタル省がStarlink端末の登録ルールを更新、KIT番号とUTIDを必須化
records.excerpt: 新しい手続きは認証要件を厳格化し、削除や情報照会の新サービスを導入します。市民や企業、外国居住者にも利用が拡大されます。 国有企業「ディア」によると。 デジタル変革省は、個人と企業向け Starlink ターミナルの登録およびレジストリからの削除手順を更新した。 Starlink の利用者向け規則を更新します – 個人および企業向け。検証には KIT-番号と UTID、またはこれらの番号のいずれかを記載する必要があります。さらに、ターミナルをレジストリから削除する新しいサービスと、登録済みデバイス情報の取得サービスを追加します – ディアの通知 認証と端末管理の主な変更 公的データによると、ポータル上でサービスを利用できるのは、法人数および独立した部門で、1年以上登録されている場合に限る。以前はアクセスには1か月以上が必要だった。端末の登録には、KIT番号とUTIDの記載が義務付けられている。 大半の企業には Starlink ターミナルの登録数が最大10台までの制限が適用されるが、重要度の高い企業には制限は適用されない。個人および個人事業主（FOP）については行政サービスセンターでの認証が利用可能。KIT番号とUTIDを準備する必要があり、これから登録されるすべての端末を提示する必要がある。以前は1台の端末を物理的な提示なしで登録できた。 ウクライナにおける一時滞在または永住許可を持つ外国人も行政サービスセンターを通じて申請できる。さらに、法人向けには、Diia ポータルを介して Starlink のターミナルをレジストリから削除するサービスが利用可能となる。これは機器を売却した場合、紛失した場合、または登録時のミスがあった場合に役立つ。削除後は別の端末を登録できる。個人および個人事業主も同様のサービスを行政サービスセンターを通じて利用できる。 法人向けには、登録済みターミナルに関する抜粋情報を取得できる新サービスが追加された。文書には、同社の全端末に関する情報が収集される。Starlink の認証は、行政サービスセンターだけでなく、ウクルポシュタの支店やノヴァポシュタの支店でも実施可能となる。FRITT UKRAINAによると、NGOの代表が国境警備局の部門向けに支援物資を提供した。支援物資には、輸送車両、充電ステーション、ドローン、Starlink のインターネット端末が含まれる。変更は、機器のより透明な管理とサービスへのアクセスの簡素化を促進することを目的としている。 この変更は、全ての利用者層に対して、機器の透明な管理とサービスへのアクセスの利便性向上を図る。 他のニュースもお見逃しなく： 政府とデジタル省がプレイシティと共同でギャンブル依存症対策ガイドを公開。早期発見のポイント、家族の寄り添い方、利用できる保護ツールと相談窓口を紹介します。

松田浩路社長が就任するタイミングでのスタートであり、値上げのタイミングと合致したことから、KDDIとしてはStarlink Directを付加価値のひとつという位置付けにしていた。そのため、誰でも使えるというわけではなく、あくまでau契約なら使えるという立ち位置にしていたのだった。 そうした路線はソフトバンクも同様だったのだが、NTTドコモは後発だったためか、付加価値という見せ方はせず、一律で無料サービスとして提供したのだった。 そんな競争もあり、KDDIはその後、UQモバイルではコミコミプランバリューととくとくプラン2利用中なら無料というかたちになった。 こうした両社の考え方の違いもあり、そもそもユーザーの母体数に大きな隔たりがあるのだ。 実際、NTTドコモでは対応機種を89機種2500万台超という言い方をしているのに対して、KDDIでは90機種1100万台超となっており、ベースの端末数でも倍以上の違いがある。 つまり、NTTドコモの500万超とKDDIの400万超を単純に比較するのはちょっと違うような気がしている。 ただ、Starlink Directは「圏外時につながる」というイメージで3社とも売り出しているだけに、いたずらに接続した数をアピールすると結果として「地上局につながらなくて困った人たち」の数と思われてしまいがちになるので、あまり訴求しないほうがいいような気がしている。 この記事の著者・石川温さんのメルマガ 初月無料で読む image by: Shutterstock.com 石川 温 この著者の記事一覧 著者：クロード、シンチャオ TechFlow 深潮導読：7月14日、JPモルガン、ゴールドマン・サックス、バンク・オブ・アメリカ、シティグループ、ウェルズ・ファーゴの五大銀行が同日、第2四半期決算を発表し、すべての指標が予想を上回った。ゴールドマン・サックスのEPSは20.98ドルで、前年比ほぼ2倍となり、株価は8％近く上昇して過去最高値を更新した。JPモルガンの純利益は212億ドルと四半期史上最高を記録した。地政学的対立による市場の激しい変動にもかかわらず、トレーディング部門は大幅な利益を上げ、SpaceXの史上最大規模のIPO（860億ドル）は投資銀行部門に巨額の手数料収入をもたらした。しかし、「予想超え」が「上昇」を意味するわけではない。シティグループはすべての業績指標が予想を上回ったにもかかわらず4.5％下落し、JPモルガンは前場で2％下落した後、反転した。モルガン・スタンレーは7月15日に決算を発表し、市場はEPSが前年比30％以上増加すると予想している。 ウォールストリートの五大行が7月14日に同日で結果を発表し、その成績は次々と驚異的だった。 ゴールドマン・サックスは企業史上最高の四半期業績を記録。モルガン・スタンレーの純利益は過去最高を更新。メリルリンチ、シティグループ、ウェルズ・ファーゴもいずれも市場予想を大幅に上回った。しかし株価の動きは大きく分かれ、ゴールドマン・サックスは8％近く上昇して過去最高値を更新した一方、シティグループは4.5％下落した。6月にはSpaceXが860億ドルを調達し、時価総額1兆7700億ドルで史上最大のIPOを実現。ほぼすべての大手証券会社が巨額の手数料を獲得した。 ゴールドマン・サックスの利益が倍増し、過去最高を記録。株価は約8%上昇。 ゴールドマン・サックスの第2四半期1株当たり利益は20.98ドルで、前年同期の10.91ドルのほぼ2倍であり、アナリスト予想の14.48ドルを大幅に上回った。純収益は203.4億ドルで、前年同期比39%増。純利益は66.3億ドルで、前年同期は37.2億ドルだった。 ブルームバーグの報道によると、ゴールドマン・サックスの株式取引部門の収益は74億2千万ドルに達し、前年同期比72％増となり、3四半期連続で過去のどの銀行も達成しなかった記録を更新した。デリバティブズ、キャッシュ製品、ブローカー業務がすべて強化された。投資銀行手数料は34億ドルで、前年同期比55％増、株式引受は130％増、債務引受は75％増となった。バロンズの報道によると、ゴールドマン・サックスは6月にSpaceXのIPOの主幹事証券会社を務めた。ブルームバーグの報道によると、同社は今年上半期にアドバイザリーを担当した公表済みのM&A取引の総額が1兆ドルを超えた。 資産・財務管理部門の収益は46億ドルで、前年同期比20%増加しました。運用資産総額は4.04兆ドルに達し、1年前は3.29兆ドルでした。ゴールドマン・サックスの取締役会は、1四半期当たりの配当を11%引き上げ、1株あたり5ドルとしました。当四半期には、株式買い戻しと配当を通じて株主に53.6億ドルを還元しました。 CEOのデビッド・ソロモンは声明で、顧客が最も戦略的な取引をゴールドマン・サックスに委託しており、これらの取引はしばしばビジネスチェーン全体の連動を促していると述べました。 Schaeffer's Investment Researchによると、ゴールドマン・サックスの株価は当日約8%上昇し、取引中で2025年4月以来の最大単日上昇幅を記録しました。今年の累計上昇幅は約27%です。 モルガン・スタンレーの四半期純利益は212億ドルと過去最高を記録したが、費用見通しの影響で前場取引で下落。 ジャパン・モルガン・チェース、第2四半期の純利益は212億ドル（1株当たり7.70ドル）と、同社史上最高の四半期利益を記録。ただし、このうち46億ドルはビザ株式の利益、10億ドルはその他の株式投資による利益を含む。一時的項目を除いた純利益は169億ドル（1株当たり6.14ドル）、前年同期比13％増。有形普通株主資本利益率（ROTCE）は23％。 収益は580億ドルで、前年同期比27%増となり、すべての事業部門で記録を更新。株式取引収益は60億ドルで、前年同期比86%大幅増。固定収益取引収益は61億ドルで、前年同期比6%増。両者合計121億ドルは、同行が2026年第1四半期に樹立した直近の取引収益記録を上回った。投資銀行手数料は33億ドルで、前年同期比30%増となり、2021年以降の最高記録を更新した。 経営陣は、年間純利息収入の見通しを1,055億ドル（前回は1,030億ドル）に引き上げたが、同時に年間調整済み費用見通しを1,075億ドルに引き上げた。後者が、取引前株価が約2%下落した主な要因となった。FX Leadersの報道によると、JPモルガンは終値で約2%上昇し、341ドルとなり、その日の反転を果たした。 ジェイミー・ディモンCEOは慎重な表現を用いた。彼は米国経済が「顕著な回復力」を示しているとし、AIへの資本支出と財政刺激が追い風になると述べたが、地政学的不安定性、インフレの粘着性、主権債務の膨張、資産価格の過大評価が「地下でプレートのように動いている」と警告した。 バンク・オブ・アメリカ、EPSが前年同期比34%増加。シティグループは10年ぶりの最高収益を記録したが、売却されるとされた。 バンク・オブ・アメリカの第2四半期1株当たり利益は1.21ドルで、前年同期比34%増、市場予想の1.12ドルを上回りました。売上高は316億ドルで、前年同期比15%増。純利益は91億ドルで、前年同期比27%増。売買取引収益は前年同期比33%増、投資銀行手数料は50%増、資産運用手数料は20%増となりました。効率比率（コスト対収益比）は59%に改善しました。CEOのブライアン・モイニハンは、消費者および企業がレジリエンスを示していると述べました。 シティグループの第2四半期1株当たり利益は3.15ドルで、20人のアナリスト全員の予想（平均予想2.74ドル）を上回った。ブルームバーグによると、売上高は248億ドルと10年ぶりの高水準となり、純利益は58億ドルで前年同期比45%増となった。株式取引収益は23億ドルで前年同期比45%増、投資銀行手数料は15.5億ドルで前年同期比44%増となった。 しかし、その日、シティグループの株価は逆に約4.5%下落しました。Investing.comの報道によると、市場の不満は、年間収益率目標（ROTCE 10%-11%）を引き上げなかったこと（年初以来すでに13.1%を達成しているにもかかわらず）に集中しています。CEOのジェーン・フレイザーは、会社が短期的な数値を美しく見せるために長期的な構築を犠牲にするのではなく、超過収益を事業に再投資することを選択したと述べました。CFOのゴンザロ・ルチェッティは、シティグループが株式事業への投資が遅れていたことを認め、競合他社に追いつくことは段階的なプロセスになると述べました。 ワシントン・ファースト銀行、第2四半期の売上高は226.2億ドルで、前年同期比8.6%増。1株当たり利益は2.00ドルで、前年同期比25%増。純利息収入は123億ドルで、前年同期比5%増。終値は0.56%微下落。 二つの触媒：地政的な変動がトレーディングデスクを満たし、SpaceXのIPOが投資銀行を満たす このラウンドの業績が予想を上回った原動力は、非常に2つの出来事に集中しています。 まず市場の変動です。米伊対立が長引いており、ホルムズ海峡の情勢が原油価格を押し上げ、株式、商品、為替市場が激しく揺れています。このような環境は銀行のトレーディング部門にとって非常に有利です。ゴールドマン・サックスの株式トレーディング収益は前年同期比72％増、JPモルガンの株式トレーディング収益は同86％増、シティグループの株式トレーディング収益は同45％増、バンク・オブ・アメリカのセールス・トレーディング収益は同33％増となりました。ブルームバーグの報道によると、五大銀行の第2四半期の合計トレーディング収益は約390億ドルに達しました。 次にSpaceXのIPOです。6月12日にSpaceXが上場し、860億ドルを調達、時価総額は1兆7700億ドルとなり、歴史上最大のIPOとなりました。ゴールドマン・サックスが主幹事証券会社を務め、JPモルガン、バンク・オブ・アメリカ、シティグループが主要な共同主幹事証券会社です。indmoneyの報道によると、主幹事手数料以外にも、各社はその後の債務調達の手配や新たな資産管理顧客の獲得から利益を得ています。A.O. ShearmanのM&A法律事務所のデータによると、2026年前半の世界のM&A取引額は2兆8000億ドルに達し、2021年以来の最高水準となりました。ゴールドマン・サックスは、Anthropicの後半期に予定されているIPOの共同アドバイザーでもあります。 モルガン・スタンレーが本日業績を発表。予想は同行によって引き上げられている。 モルガン・スタンレーは7月15日（本日）の市場開前にQ2決算を発表します。 Zacksのデータによると、一致予想EPSは約2.89ドル（過去1週間で4%上方修正）、前年同期比で約35.7%の成長見込みです。売上高予想は約1934億ドルで、前年同期比で約16.9%の成長が見込まれています。昨日（7月14日）、モルガン・スタンレーは業界全体が予想を上回った影響で約4%上昇しましたが、同社自身の決算はまだ発表されていません。 前四半期のモルガン・スタンレーのEPSは3.43ドルと大幅に市場予想を上回り、売上高は206億ドルで前年同期比16%増、株式取引収益は52億ドルで前年同期比25%増となった。財務管理部門は1,180億ドルの新規資産を獲得した。同業他社の業績を踏まえると、市場はモルガン・スタンレーが予想を上回ると見込んでいたが、その予想自体はすでに引き上げられていた。オッペンハイマーのアナリスト、クリス・コトウスキーは6月30日に評価を「市場を下回る」に引き下げており、これは現在でも少数派の悲観的見方である。

records.title: SpaceX bears are taking a victory lap as the stock struggles a month after the IPO
records.excerpt: SpaceX dipped below its IPO price this week. The bears says it reinforces their view that the stock was overvalued and that more pain may be coming. SpaceX stock has struggled after a brief burst of post-IPO enthusiasm, and the bears are taking a moment to reiterate their downbeat views on the stock. A month after a historic IPO, SpaceX stock dropped below the initial offering price of $135 on Wednesday, marking a 40% decline from its peak of around $225. Wall Street analysts rushed to issue bullish price targets when the stock joined the Nasdaq 100 earlier this month, but the bears are feeling emboldened by the plunge that they say bolsters the view that the stock was overvalued from the get-go. "Expect the price to completely crash," former Fidelity Overseas Fund manager and hedge fund founder George Noble told Business Insider. "I think it could be half over the course of the year." Noble said $30 is a fair price target for SpaceX stock, a forecast that implies a drop of 78% from Wednesday's price. He's also previously criticized Tesla, describing Musk's EV company as the biggest bubble in stock market history. Jay Ritter, an economist and market commentator dubbed "Mr. IPO" for his expertise and research on companies and capital markets, told Business Insider that he was considering shorting SpaceX prior to its IPO. While Ritter didn't say whether he is betting against the stock yet, he added that he's not at all surprised by the post-IPO slide. CFRA analyst Keith Snyder labeled the stock with a "sell" rating directly following its IPO and hasn't wavered, even as many of his peers on Wall Street dole out bullish price targets and commentary in their initial coverage. "I am still negative on the valuation at these levels and haven't seen anything that would change the story for me," Snyder told Business Insider last week. The only thing he says would change his mind is actual growth. Ed Elson, a day trader who co-hosts Scott Galloway's Prof G Markets podcast, said in June that he saw the stock as highly overvalued, predicting that it would be cut in half within the coming year. On July 14, Elson shared an updated take on SpaceX, highlighting concerns about the bullish sentiment among Wall Street analysts. Elson laid out why this may be problematic for investors, especially as many bullish analysts are from banks that underwrote the SpaceX IPO. In his view, they still have financial incentive to describe the stock favorably, even after the end of the legal 'quiet period' for underwriters. "Anyone who bought post-IPO is now underwater," he said. "This is in line with the trend: Research shows IPOs recommended by analysts at underwriting banks underperform and, on average, lose value."

records.excerpt: SpaceX below IPO price as rally that made Elon Musk a trillionaire fizzles Email New York Post Switch between CA and NY editions here. Edition Recommended Skip to main content Business SpaceX shares drop below $135 IPO price as rally that made Elon Musk a trillionaire fizzles By Reuters Published July 15, 2026 Updated July 15, 2026, 4:15 p.m. ET See more of our coverage in your search results. Add The New York Post on Google SpaceX shares dropped below their initial public offering price on Wednesday, a first for the company, just over a month after a frenzy over the rockets-to-AI firm powered the biggest IPO ever and made Elon Musk the world’s first trillionaire . Shares hit a record low of $132.15, falling below the $135 apiece IPO price and well below the all-time high of $225.64, which propelled the company’s market valuation briefly above those of Silicon Valley giants Microsoft and Amazon. The stock later rebounded to close at $135.27, down 0.6%. Many contended the stock’s rally was likely vulnerable to reversals, given SpaceX’s $4.9 billion in net losses last year and the uncertainty over the firm’s prospects as well as the stock valuations that might hold across the market at a time when inflation has been rising, putting the Fed’s policymakers on notice. 3 SpaceX shares dropped below their initial public offering price on Wednesday. Above, SpaceX leadership and guests celebrate at the Nasdaq on the first day of trading on June 12. REUTERS The decline leaves investors who bought into the company at the IPO price sitting on paper losses for the first time, potentially testing confidence in the stock. It also offers a reminder that Wall Street enthusiasm can cool quickly , even for a company with the size and scale of SpaceX, which raised around $85.7 billion and fetched a valuation of around $2.1 trillion at the end of its first trading day. It is not uncommon for a stock to fall below the IPO price, especially during periods of broader market stress. Wall Street’s main indexes have been under pressure in recent weeks due to uncertainty around the Federal Reserve’s interest rate path and concerns about the durability of the rally powered by AI winners such as chipmakers. Still, the drop may bolster critics who had argued that SpaceX’s valuation was stretched, as the company was unprofitable and many of its ambitious bets were still untested. Investors would find better entry points after the first wave of excitement had faded, some analysts had warned before the IPO. 3 The Spacex IPO made Elon Musk the world’s first trillionaire. REUTERS 3 SpaceX’s shares have dropped nearly 13% since they were included in the Nasdaq 100. REUTERS The reversal also underscores the risks of chasing momentum, and the limits of a valuation driven more by narrative than near-term fundamentals. The stock’s addition to prestigious indexes, such as the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100, did little to reignite the buying. SpaceX’s shares have dropped nearly 13% since they were included in the Nasdaq 100. The focus now shifts to the company’s first results after listing. SpaceX has not yet disclosed when it plans to do it, but has said they will be released only through its website and ‌its social media account on X, and not through wire distribution services.

records.title: SpaceX shares fall below IPO price for first time
records.excerpt: SpaceX’s stock price has fallen below its listing price of $135 (£100) for the first time since its blockbuster Wall Street flotation last month. SpaceX shares fall below IPO price for first time Louis Goss Wed, July 15, 2026 at 12:41 PM EDT 3 min read SPCX SpaceX's shares fall below the $135 level of its initial public offering - Spencer Platt/Getty SpaceX's stock price has fallen below its listing price of $135 (£100) for the first time since its blockbuster Wall Street flotation last month. Shares in Elon Musk's rocket company fell to all-time lows of $132 per share on Monday, extending a steep decline over the last month. SpaceX shares surged in the week after its historic public debut , which valued the company at $1.77tn, making it the biggest ever initial public offering. The company's stock price was bid higher in a frenzy of trading as retail investors around the world sought to gain exposure to the company. SpaceX stock peaked at almost $214 per share on June 17. However, shares have since slipped by over 38pc, knocking more than $800bn in value off the Texas headquartered conglomerate. SpaceX's share price later recovered to just over $135 by the end of Wednesday's trading session on the New York Stock Exchange. Mr Musk, who owns a 42pc stake in SpaceX, became a trillionaire when the company joined the stock market. However, his total wealth has since fallen to around $861bn as SpaceX has declined. Most observers believe SpaceX's falling share price reflects fading hype for the company, as early investors who sought to make a quick return cash out the stock. However, the fall below the initial public offering (IPO) price came as Mr Musk said Marine Le Pen was "France's last hope" in a post on his social media platform X on Wednesday. Mr Musk has previously backed Ms Le Pen, the hard Right populist leader, but this is the first time he has done so since she officially re-entered the race to replace centrist president Emmanuel Macron in elections next year. Entrepreneur Mr Musk has frequently weighed in on European politics in recent years, supporting far-Right politicians . He has repeatedly criticised Sir Keir Starmer and voiced support for Rupert Lowe, the leader of Restore Britain. In February last year, Mr Musk also congratulated Alice Weidel, the co-leader of Alternative for Germany (AfD), after her party came second in Germany's elections. As well as building and launching rockets and satellites, Mr Musk has expanded SpaceX into AI through the acquisition of his company xAI, which owns the chatbot Grok and the social media network X. Last month, SpaceX also struck a $60bn deal to buy Cursor, an AI coding startup founded by four former MIT students in 2022. It transformed Cursor's founders, who are all in their 20s, into multibillionaires. SpaceX was started by Mr Musk in 2002 with the aim of making low-cost, reusable rockets. It later made history with the launch of its Falcon 1 rocket, which became the first ever privately-funded vehicle to successfully reach the Earth's orbit in 2008. The company has since made more than 600 launches into orbit, including sending satellites into space for the Starlink network, which provides high-speed broadband to remote areas. SpaceX has said it eventually aims to build fully reusable rockets capable of carrying passengers to Mars. Its rockets have also helped deliver supplies and packages to the International Space Station. The slump in SpaceX's share price coincided with broader selling of chipmakers. It saw shares in America's biggest chip makers drop sharply on Wednesday, with Micron Technology shares falling by more than 7pc and Intel shares dropping by 5pc. South Korean chip makers also slumped, with SK Hynix shares plunging by 10pc and Samsung Electronics shares falling by 9pc. Bank of America's fund managers survey on Wednesday showed investors cut their exposure to technology companies this month to shield themselves against risks surrounding a possible AI bubble. Amazon to launch S.Africa satellite internet as Starlink awaits licence AFP Wed, July 15, 2026 at 1:51 PM EDT 1 min read AMZN SPCX Amazon launched its first batch of low-Earth orbit satellites last year (JUSTIN TALLIS) Amazon said Wednesday it will launch satellite internet services in South Africa, entering a market where rival Elon Musk's Starlink has struggled to secure regulatory approval. Amazon Leo, the US e-commerce giant's low-Earth orbit satellite network, aims to provide internet access to customers in areas with limited or no connectivity. The company, founded by American billionaire Jeff Bezos, will partner with South African internet provider Herotel, it said on its website. Under the deal, Herotel -- South Africa's largest fixed internet service provider -- will use Amazon Leo's technology to offer a new service called Evry, slated for launch commercially in 2027. "This is the first Amazon Leo agreement of this kind in Africa," the company said, without disclosing financial terms. The announcement comes as SpaceX's Starlink has yet to secure a licence in South Africa because of local ownership rules. Telecoms companies in South Africa, including those with foreign investment, are required to provide 30 percent equity to historically disadvantaged groups -- a policy created to mitigate the legacy of racial inequality left by apartheid. South Africa-born billionaire Musk has refused to cede ownership stakes, calling the black empowerment policy "openly racist". Musk, who left South Africa in his late teens, has repeatedly accused the Pretoria government of discriminating against white people. Amazon launched its first batch of low-Earth orbit satellites last year and says it now has more than 390 satellites deployed, far behind Starlink's fleet of more than 10,000. ho/rh Terms and Privacy Policy Your Privacy Choices More Info

records.excerpt: SpaceX shares fell below their $135 IPO price for the first time on Wednesday, leaving investors in Elon Musk's rocket company with paper losses. Table of Contents SpaceX shares dropped below their initial public offering price for the first time on Wednesday, leaving investors who bought into the record listing sitting on paper losses just over a month after the debut that made Elon Musk the world's first trillionaire. The stock fell as much as 2.9% to $132.15 during the session, breaking beneath the $135 a share at which the company sold stock in June, before recovering to close at $135.27. It was the fourth straight session of declines and the lowest level the shares have touched since the rocket, satellite and artificial intelligence company went public. The drop marks a sharp reversal from the frenzy that greeted the listing. SpaceX raised about $86 billion in the biggest IPO in history on June 12, then watched its stock surge nearly 50% over the first three days of trading, peaking near $214 on June 17 and briefly carrying a valuation above $2.6 trillion, more than Microsoft or Amazon. It has lost value in almost every week since. The unwinding has erased an enormous sum. From its high, the stock has fallen more than 38%, wiping over $800 billion off the company's value. SpaceX was worth about $1.75 trillion on Wednesday afternoon, down from the $2.6 trillion peak reached weeks earlier. Musk's fortune has moved with it. Forbes estimated his net worth at about $856.8 billion on Wednesday, down sharply from a high of $1.45 trillion shortly after the debut. He remains the richest person in the world by a wide margin, and he controls the company through a stake variously reported at 38% to 42% and a dominant share of the voting rights, so the selloff costs him money but not control. Part of the volatility is structural. Only about 4% of SpaceX's shares trade on the Nasdaq, an unusually small float that, combined with relentless attention on the company, has produced wild swings. Thinly traded stocks move further on each buy and sell order, and analysts say early investors cashing out to lock in gains have added downward pressure. The rest reflects a change in mood. Markets have cooled on the artificial intelligence trade that lifted SpaceX and its peers, with investors moving from what one analyst called pricing in promise toward closer scrutiny of the companies actually linked to AI. SpaceX has staked much of its valuation on that theme. It acquired Musk's AI startup xAI in an all-stock deal in February, spent $7.7 billion on AI-related capital expenditure in the first quarter, roughly three-quarters of its total, and has told regulators it could deploy space-based data centers as early as 2028. The company's induction into the Nasdaq-100 last week, achieved under a rule change that shortened the eligibility window for newly public companies to 15 trading days, brought passive index funds into the stock but did not halt the slide. The shares fell below their first-day trading level within a day of joining the index. Wall Street analysts remain broadly bullish despite the drop. The consensus price target sits around $247, well above the current level, with roughly 80% of analysts rating the stock a buy or overweight. Supporters argue the valuation reflects years of large investments still to come, and that the company's ambitions in launch, satellite internet and AI justify patience. Skeptics counter that the price ran far ahead of the fundamentals. Beneath the market drama, SpaceX's core business continues to generate the revenue that underpins the valuation. Starlink, its satellite internet service, is the largest contributor, and it has expanded across much of the world, including more than two dozen African markets. The service remains unavailable in South Africa, the country of Musk's birth, where it has not met a requirement that licensees be at least 30% owned by historically disadvantaged groups, a standoff Musk has publicly criticized. The selloff comes at a sensitive moment. SpaceX is due to launch the 13th test flight of its Starship rocket on Thursday, carrying Starlink satellites that will attempt to connect with ground stations in South Africa. The share price has become a real-time referendum on the ambitions Musk has attached to the company, and a prolonged downturn could ripple outward, weighing on the bonds SpaceX sold after the IPO and setting a cautious tone for the listings of other AI-linked giants, including Anthropic and OpenAI, both of which have filed confidentially to go public. Whether Wednesday's dip hardens into a sustained decline or proves another swing in a volatile first month will shape how those offerings are received. What has already changed is the story investors tell about SpaceX. A month ago it was the hottest debut in market history. It is now a stock trading below the price at which it sold. records.title: Missed Out On The SpaceX IPO? Buy These Industrial Giants Instead.
records.excerpt: Investors can gain exposure to the space boom through established defense contractors benefiting from Golden Dome spending without relying on SpaceX alone. Missed Out On The SpaceX IPO? Buy These Industrial Giants Instead. Micah Zimmerman, The Motley Fool Wed, July 15, 2026 at 3:25 AM EDT 5 min read SPCX NVDA Space Exploration Technologies ' (NASDAQ: SPCX) IPO was the hottest ticket of the year, and if you didn't get a piece, the fear of missing out is real. But here's something the frenzy overlooked: You don't need SpaceX to invest in space. A handful of established industrial giants are cashing in on the same boom, and they come with steadier businesses and, in most cases, a dividend check while you wait. There's a powerful tailwind behind them, too -- the U.S. government's push to build a space-based missile shield known as Golden Dome, which is funneling tens of billions of dollars toward satellites, sensors, and rockets. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » 1. Lockheed Martin: The space and defense anchor Lockheed Martin (NYSE: LMT) is about as close to a one-stop shop for national-security space as you'll find. It builds satellites, missile-warning systems, and the Orion crew capsule, and late last year it won a roughly $1.1 billion award to deliver 18 missile-tracking satellites for the Space Force. It's also positioned at the center of the Golden Dome effort. This is the blue chip way to own the government side of the space race. 2. Northrop Grumman: Satellites and the propulsion nobody sees Northrop Grumman (NYSE: NOC) is deep in the same satellite constellations, having won its own multi-hundred-million-dollar Space Force awards, with a batch of its data-relay satellites slated to begin launching this year. What I find underappreciated is its propulsion business: Northrop makes solid rocket motors that power missiles and launch vehicles across the industry, so it profits no matter whose rocket flies. 3. L3Harris Technologies: The sensor specialist L3Harris Technologies (NYSE: LHX) rounds out the group that split the Space Force's latest missile-tracking satellite contract, and its real strength lies in the sensors and payloads that enable those satellites to actually spot a threat. The company has been sharpening its focus lately, agreeing to sell a majority stake in its space-propulsion arm to concentrate on the electronics and space systems where it has an edge. For a Golden Dome built on detection, that's a smart place to sit. 4. RTX: Missiles, sensors, and a missile-defense windfall RTX (NYSE: RTX), parent company of Raytheon and Collins Aerospace, is one of the largest defense contractors on Earth, and missile defense is squarely in its wheelhouse. The interceptors and radars that would form the lower layers of a system like Golden Dome are the kind of hardware RTX has made for decades. Its aerospace arm also supplies components across satellites and spacecraft, giving it broad, if less pure, space exposure. Image source: Getty Images. 5. Boeing: The direct launch competitor Boeing (NYSE: BA) is the wild card here, and I'll be candid: It's the most troubled company on this list . But it co-owns United Launch Alliance, whose Vulcan rocket competes head-to-head with SpaceX for the most sensitive national-security launches, and it retains a large defense and space portfolio. If you believe the government wants more than one launch provider, and it clearly does, Boeing offers direct exposure to that rivalry, provided you can stomach its ongoing turnaround risk. The takeaway worth understanding Now the honest counterweight: None of these companies is a substitute for SpaceX in terms of growth. They're large, mature businesses where space is only one slice of the pie, so a satellite win rarely moves the whole stock the way it might for a pure play. Their fortunes also lean heavily on government budgets, and programs like Golden Dome depend on appropriations that politics can slow, shrink, or reroute. Defense primes can also trade at rich valuations when geopolitical worries run hot, as they do now. If you're chasing SpaceX-style rocket-ship returns, these steady industrials won't scratch that itch. But if what you actually wanted was durable exposure to the money pouring into space and missile defense, this group delivers it without the hype. My honest suggestion is to treat them as the sensible, lower-drama way to invest in the theme and lean toward the names with the clearest space and Golden Dome tailwinds rather than buying all five indiscriminately. The shares declined 2.2% on Tuesday to close at $13… SpaceX Drops 33%, Nears IPO Price Despite 70% Analyst Upside 2 min read SPCX SpaceX SPCX , Elon Musk's rocket, satellite and artificial intelligence company, has moved close to its $135 initial public offering price after three consecutive sessions of losses raised fresh questions about near-term investor confidence. The shares declined 2.2% on Tuesday to close at $136.08, leaving them only $1 above the price paid by IPO investors last month. SpaceX has now fallen about one-third from its post-listing peak, erasing nearly $850 billion in market value. Investors often monitor the IPO price as an important psychological level because a decline below it shortly after a listing may put early shareholders in the red and weaken the carefully built enthusiasm surrounding a new issue. The latest decline comes despite a strongly positive response from Wall Street following SpaceX's addition to the Nasdaq-100 through fast-entry rules. More than a dozen banks, including Morgan Stanley, a global financial services firm, JPMorgan Chase, a major U.S. banking group, and Goldman Sachs, a global investment bank, began coverage with buy-equivalent ratings. More than 80% of analysts following SpaceX recommend buying the shares, while their average price target of $236.25 suggests potential upside of more than 70% from Tuesday's closing level. However, some investors remain cautious because SpaceX trades at a forward estimated price-to-sales ratio above 30 times, among the highest in the Nasdaq-100 and only modestly below Palantir Technologies, a company referenced in the source as a valuation comparison. The company also faces an extended lock-up structure that is expected to release insider shares into the market periodically over the coming months, which could increase available supply. The weakness in SpaceX also reflects the volatility affecting several of the largest U.S. listings this year. Bloomberg data show that six of the 10 biggest offerings are trading below their first-day closing levels, while the weighted-average return for 2026 U.S. IPOs excluding blank-check companies had fallen to 5.3% through July 13. A Truist Wealth analysis of 30 major technology IPOs over the previous 15 years found that those stocks experienced an average maximum decline of 55% during their first year of trading, suggesting that sharp early pullbacks are not unusual for newly public technology companies. Investors are also watching American depositary shares of SK Hynix (HXSCL), a South Korean chipmaker, after SpaceX and SK Hynix completed record-setting listings less than one month apart. A decline below SpaceX's IPO price may attract investors who missed the original offering, although Ken Mahoney of Mahoney Asset Management said the shares may not yet have reached their low, while Talley Leger of the Wealth Consulting Group indicated that a deeper pullback could make the stock more attractive. records.excerpt: The $135 Price Tag Is Not About Valuation — It's About Control SpaceX is reportedly pricing its IPO at $135 per share ahead of a landmark Starship launch. Every financial outlet will frame this as a valuation story. That's the wrong frame entirely. What the $135 number actually reveals is the most sophisticated business model The $135 Price Tag Is Not About Valuation — It's About Control SpaceX is reportedly pricing its IPO at $135 per share ahead of a landmark Starship launch. Every financial outlet will frame this as a valuation story. That's the wrong frame entirely. What the $135 number actually reveals is the most sophisticated business model sequencing play in modern tech — and it has almost nothing to do with going public in the traditional sense. SpaceX doesn't need capital. Starlink alone generates enough recurring subscription revenue to fund operations at a scale most aerospace companies can only dream about. So why price an IPO at all? Because pricing is a signal — and SpaceX is using it to send a very specific one to three different audiences simultaneously. SpaceX vs. Boeing: Two Business Models, One Industry — One Winner To understand what SpaceX is really doing, compare it to Boeing's business model trajectory. Boeing built itself around government contracts, certification dependency, and legacy manufacturing — a cost-plus model where complexity is revenue. SpaceX inverted this entirely. It built a vertical integration flywheel: manufacture the rockets, own the launches, own the satellite network, own the internet subscriptions at the edge. Every layer of the stack that SpaceX owns is a layer Boeing couldn't charge for.Business Engineerhow SpaceX is rewriting the Map of AI infrastructureRead → The IPO price at $135 — deliberately modest relative to its last private valuation — does something elegant: it creates a secondary market without surrendering board control, keeps institutional appetite high while Musk retains operational authority, and positions Starlink as the "boring profitable core" that justifies the valuation while Starship gets to remain the moonshot narrative. This is a dual-narrative business model: one entity funds the other while carrying two different investor stories. The Starship Launch Is the Real IPO Roadshow Timing matters here. The IPO price drops just as a Starship launch is imminent. This is not coincidence — it's the oldest business model move in hardware tech: ship the demo when the money is on the table. Apple did it with iPhone. Tesla did it with every quarterly delivery surge timed before raises. SpaceX is doing it at planetary scale. What Starship actually represents in business model terms is a cost-per-kilogram collapse. If Starship reaches full reusability at scale, the cost to orbit drops by an order of magnitude. That's not just an aerospace achievement — it's a platform shift. The same way AWS turned Amazon's infrastructure costs into a product, Starship turns SpaceX's launch economics into a business model moat that no competitor can replicate for at least a decade. For a deeper breakdown of how platform moats get built around infrastructure costs, see the platform business model framework and the vertical integration strategy guide on FourWeekMBA. The Three-Layer SpaceX Business Model Nobody Explains Strip away the Musk narrative and SpaceX operates across three distinct business model layers that interact in ways most analysts miss: Business EngineerProduct Overhang Doctrine — why AI disrupts in burstsRead → Layer 1 — Launch-as-a-Service: Government and commercial contracts (NASA, DoD, private satellites). High margin, non-recurring, prestige-anchoring. This is what built SpaceX's credibility and balance sheet. Layer 2 — Starlink Subscriptions: Recurring consumer and enterprise internet revenue. This is the cash engine. Low churn in underserved markets, military contracts layered on top. This is what funds everything else. Layer 3 — Starship Infrastructure Platform: The future lever. If Starship works at scale, SpaceX becomes the AWS of space — selling access to orbit the way Amazon sells access to compute. This layer doesn't exist yet as a revenue line, but it's what the $135 IPO price is actually pricing in. Most IPO analysis gets stuck at Layer 1. The market is pricing Layer 2. Musk is building Layer 3. Bold Prediction: SpaceX Goes Public to Lock In the Narrative, Not the Capital Here's the thesis that no financial outlet will publish: SpaceX is using the IPO as a business model communication tool, not a fundraising mechanism. The $135 price point is calibrated to be "reasonable" — not a blockbuster pop, not a disappointing flat. It keeps SpaceX out of the "overhyped IPO" narrative while locking in a public market reference price that validates Starlink's subscription model as a standalone business worth hundreds of billions. Once that reference price exists, every future Starship milestone becomes a re-rating event. Every government contract, every Starlink subscriber milestone, every successful heavy-lift launch moves the stock — and the narrative. The IPO isn't the destination. It's the distribution mechanism for the next decade of SpaceX storytelling. That's the business model Elon Musk is actually building. And $135 is just the opening line. records.excerpt: Here’s how much SpaceX stock crashed below its IPO price Skip to content Here’s how much SpaceX stock crashed below its IPO price Marko Stocks Jul 16, 2026 SpaceX (NASDAQ: SPCX ) stock fell below its initial public offering ( IPO ) price of $135 for the first time on Wednesday, July 15. The stock dropped as low as $132.28 during the session as investors reassessed the company’s valuation, before it recovered slightly to close at $135.27. At the current price, SpaceX shares are more or less back at the IPO price. However, they are down roughly 16% from their closing price of $160 on June 12, when the space company went public, and about 36% from the record price of around $211 on June 16. Now, the company has a market cap of $1.78 trillion, marking a notable retreat from the $2.9 trillion recorded just four days after the IPO. SpaceX stock price chart (1M). Source: Finbold SpaceX stock price continues to decline The decline highlights how quickly investor enthusiasm can fade, even for a company backed by Elon Musk and involved with key growth narratives such as artificial intelligence ( AI ). Primarily, the selloff comes as investors reassess SpaceX’s valuation and financial outlook as the first earnings date in August draws near. Among the key concerns is SpaceX’s $4.9 billion net loss in 2025 as heavy investment in AI infrastructure and Starship development weighed on its bottom line. The stock’s inclusion in the NASDAQ 100 failed to reverse the decline, with shares down about 13% since joining the index. Analysts expect SpaceX’s revenue to reach between $34 billion and $43 billion this year (versus $18.7 billion in 2025), supported by continued Starlink subscriber growth and expanding AI computing contracts. However, investors are also preparing for a potential increase in selling pressure in late 2026. Notably, insider share unlocks expected after the company reports its second-quarter results in August could significantly increase the public float, allowing eligible employees and early investors to sell portions of their holdings. Still, SpaceX remains among the top ten largest publicly traded companies in the world. PHOTO: REUTERS SPACEX shares slumped to their lowest level since the rocket, satellite, and artificial intelligence company went public, briefly falling below their initial public offering price, as investor fanfare quickly evaporated in the month since its trading debut. The stock fell 0.6 per cent to close at US$135.27 on Wednesday (Jul 15), ending the day just above the US$135 per share level that SpaceX sold them to investors in June as [part of a record US$86 billion offering](https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/international/global/spacex-ipo-raises-us75-billion-biggest-debut-all-time) after slumping below the key level intraday. It was the fourth consecutive day of declines for the stock. A company’s shares falling below the IPO price within days or weeks of its first trading day punctures the narrative that has been carefully choreographed by the company and its bankers to hype up expectations. Putting shareholders in the red at such an early stage is a blow to confidence that some newly-listed firms do not recover from. SpaceX shares have been subject to volatility usually associated with new IPOs, surging nearly 50 per cent over their first three days of trading, only to [lose nearly a quarter of their value](https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/international/global/spacex-falls-third-day-erases-us600-billion-market-value) over the next three sessions. “Investors are becoming more cognisant that much of SpaceX is about its xAI ambitions,” said Dec Mullarkey, managing director at SLC Management. “As markets get more cautious on the cost and efficacy of the intensive buildout, SpaceX plans may sound too far removed from immediate cash flow,” he added. ## More downside pressure There could be more pain ahead too. The first of many share lockups that have kept early investors from selling shares are set to expire once the company reports its first set of quarterly results – something it must do in the coming weeks. The stock also became a member of the Russell 1000 Index in late June, just two weeks after its IPO. Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Rob Du Boff estimated that SpaceX’s inclusion in the Nasdaq 100 and FTSE Russell gauges would drive at least US$5.4 billion in buying from index funds. Of course, being included in the indexes could be putting extra downside pressure on SpaceX shares also swept up in the artificial intelligence trade. It will be the first Starship flight since May’s booster failure. The company does not plan to reuse any parts during this flight: they will be modeled to land in the Gulf of Mexico, so both parts of the system are intended to end with an explosion. records.title: Will next SpaceX rocket launch be seen in Arizona? How to see Falcon 9
records.excerpt: Title: Will next SpaceX rocket launch be seen in Arizona? How to see Falcon 9 URL Source: http://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/arizona/2026/07/13/spacex-falcon-9-launch-today-arizona/90874856007/ Published Time: 2026-07-13T16:01:11Z Markdown Content: July 13, 2026, 9:01 a.m. MT * The rocket's southeastern trajectory means it should be visible from neighboring Arizona. * Set for July 13, this mission will carry 24 of SpaceX's Starlink internet satellites into low-Earth orbit. * The launch can be watched via a live webcast on the SpaceX website. Get ready, Arizona: SpaceX's next [rocket launch from neighboring California](https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/california/2026/06/25/vandenberg-rocket-launch-spacex-photos/90690138007/) is primed to be an easy one to see across state lines. For the fourth time in July, [SpaceX is planning to launch](https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/california/2026/06/23/vandenberg-demolition-spacex-launch-complex/90640516007/) its Falcon 9 rocket from the [Vandenberg Space Force Base](https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/california/2026/06/16/new-vandenberg-site-rocket-launches-california-spacex/90555488007/). Once again, the 230-foot rocket will be getting off the ground on a mission to transport the [spaceflight company](https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/california/2026/07/02/spacex-unveils-starmind-latest-addition-to-growing-list-of-cosmic-names/90765671007/)'s [Starlink internet satellites](https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/2025/07/23/spacex-rocket-launch-starlink-satellites-california-florida/85324371007/) to Earth orbit. And for Arizonans [eager to see the rocket](https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/california/2026/07/13/next-vandenberg-rocket-launch-spacex-today/90874730007/), it's good news: a southeastern trajectory will take the Falcon 9 [right across the state](https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/arizona/2026/07/10/spacex-rocket-launch-today-vandenberg-arizona/90858844007/). Keep in mind that postponements due to weather or issues with rockets are common with spaceflight. If you're going to try to spot the rocket launch, check back with [azcentral.com](http://www.azcentral.com/) for any updates on the mission. [![Image 1](https://www.azcentral.com/gcdn/authoring/authoring-images/2025/10/07/PPHX/86557190007-blast-off-space-x-seen-from-carefree-arizona-in-sept-2025-provided-by-eric-lindblad.jpg?crop=1918,1080,x0,y0&width=660&height=372&format=pjpg&auto=webp)](https://www.azcentral.com/picture-gallery/news/local/arizona-science/2025/10/15/space-x-rocket-launches/86695240007/) In the meantime, here's [what to know about the launch from neighboring California](https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/california/2026/07/13/spacex-rocket-launch-schedule-vandenberg/90873937007/), as well as when and where to potentially see the rocket in Arizona. ## Is there a rocket launch today? Next mission from Vandenberg in California [SpaceX is working toward](https://www.spacex.com/launches/sl-15-14) a Monday, July 13, launch from Southern California, with a one-hour launch window opening at 6:16 p.m. PT. A Federal Aviation Administration operations [plan advisory](https://www.fly.faa.gov/adv/adv_spt.jsp)suggests a backup opportunity is available the next day if the launch were to be postponed. [![Image 2](https://www.azcentral.com/gcdn/authoring/authoring-images/2026/06/29/PBRE/90735167007-falcon-9.jpg?crop=1619,911,x0,y162&width=660&height=372&format=pjpg&auto=webp)](https://www.azcentral.com/picture-gallery/news/local/california/2026/02/03/rocket-launches-vandenberg-falcon-9/88487613007/) ## Will SpaceX rocket launch be visible in Arizona? What to know about trajectory The launch will take place from Space Launch Complex 4-East (SLC-4E,) which SpaceX leases as a launch site for its Falcon 9 rocket at the [Vandenberg Space Force Base in Santa Barbara County](https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/2025/06/10/california-rocket-launch-vandenberg-base/84128076007/). Because the rocket is due to [fly at a southeastern trajectory](https://nextspaceflight.com/launches/details/8298/), it may be easier to spot in Arizona. [![Image 3](https://www.azcentral.com/gcdn/authoring/authoring-images/2025/06/17/PPHX/84240877007-img-3141.jpg?crop=4031,2269,x0,y377&width=660&height=372&format=pjpg&auto=webp)](https://www.azcentral.com/picture-gallery/news/local/arizona/2025/06/17/spacex-launch-photos/84240918007/) ## How to watch SpaceX launch livestream Fortunately for those in Arizona interested in watching the launch, SpaceX also provides a live webcast of its missions. The launch will be available to stream on the company's [website](https://www.spacex.com/launches/sl-15-14) and its new X TV mobile app, beginning about five minutes before liftoff. SpaceX may also provide updates on[social media site X](https://x.com/SpaceX?ref_src=twsrc%5Egoogle%7Ctwcamp%5Eserp%7Ctwgr%5Eauthor). ## What is the Vandenberg rocket launch? Falcon 9 to deploy Starlink satellites SpaceX will launch its famous two-stage 230-foot [Falcon 9](https://www.spacex.com/vehicles/falcon-9/) rocket, one of the world's most active, to [deliver 24 Starlink satellites](https://www.spacex.com/launches/sl-15-14) into low-Earth orbit, an altitude nearer Earth's atmosphere where they're able to circle the planet quickly. ## Where to watch SpaceX Falcon 9 in Arizona Because of Arizona's proximity to the launch site, there's a good chance people there can see the spacecraft streak across the sky, especially at night or very early morning. Here's a list of some possible viewing locations compiled by The Arizona Republic, a USA TODAY Network publication. * **Dobbins Lookout**,[South Mountain](https://www.phoenix.gov/administration/departments/parks/activities-facilities/trails/south-mountain-parkpreserve.html), 10919 S. Central Ave., Phoenix, Arizona * **Papago Park**, 625 N. Galvin Parkway, Phoenix, Arizona * **Fountain Hills**, a town in Maricopa County, Arizona, which in 2018 [was designated a Dark Sky Community](https://darksky.org/places/fountain-hills-arizona-dark-sky-community/)with little light pollution * **Superstition Mountains**,[located 40 miles from](https://www.visitphoenix.com/sonoran-desert/parks/superstition-mountains/)metro Phoenix in Arizona * **Cave Creek**,[a town in Maricopa County](https://www.cavecreekaz.gov/)about 30 miles north of Fountain Hills, Arizona * [**Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport**](https://www.skyharbor.com/), 3400 Sky Harbor Blvd., Arizona, which has a parking garage that is popular for plane-watching * **Black Canyon City**, an unincorporated community in Yavapai County, Arizona * Any mountain park in Arizona * **[Estrella Mountain Regional Park](https://www.maricopacountyparks.net/park-locator/estrella-mountain-regional-park/)**, 14805 W. Phillips Road, Queen Creek, Arizona * **Monument Hill**,[a 150-foot slope](https://www.kjzz.org/2013-12-13/content-13073-did-you-know-monument-hill-important-arizona-spot)on 115th Avenue, in Arizona * **Casa Grande**,a city in Pinal County, approximately halfway between Phoenix and Tucson * **Avondale**, a city in Maricopa County bordering Phoenix to the west * **Queen Creek**, a suburb of Phoenix ## Photos of SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket in Arizona, US [![Image 4](http://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/arizona/2026/07/13/spacex-falcon-9-launch-today-arizona/90874856007/)](https://www.azcentral.com/picture-gallery/news/local/arizona/2025/05/26/spacex-falcon-nine-rocket-launch-california-seen-arizona-skies/10620445002/

records.title: SpaceX Falcon 9 launches 29 Starlink satellites from Cape Canaveral
records.excerpt: SpaceX successfully deployed another batch of Starlink internet satellites from Florida early Tuesday morning with a Falcon 9 rocket. Skip to content SpaceX Falcon 9 launches 29 Starlink satellites from Cape Canaveral Published on 14 July 2026 at 5:38 am • Written by Chris Martin • Reading duration : 2 minutes · read 40 times © SpaceX Falcon 9 launches 29 Starlink satellites from Cape Canaveral Post on Facebook Post on Flipboard Share on LinkedIn Post on Reddit Share on Telegram Share on X Send through Whatsapp SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 rocket carrying 29 Starlink satellites into orbit from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station early Tuesday, July 14, continuing the company’s rapid pace of rocket launches. Liftoff occurred at 5:10 a.m. EDT from Launch Complex 40, with the mission designated Starlink 10-45. The booster completed its 28th flight, adding to SpaceX’s growing record of rocket reuse. Previous missions flown by the same first stage include Axiom 2, Euclid, Axiom 3, the CRS-30 International Space Station resupply mission, SES ASTRA 1P, the NG-21 ISS resupply mission, and 21 Starlink missions, according to Florida Today. After deploying the satellites, the first stage landed on the A Shortfall of Gravitas drone ship in the Atlantic Ocean. The Starlink constellation has grown substantially through 2026. As of June 2026, the network consisted of approximately 10,413 satellites in low Earth orbit, with 10,397 operational, according to Wikipedia. SpaceX had reported more than 9,600 Starlink broadband and mobile satellites in low Earth orbit as of March 31, 2026, indicating rapid expansion of the network’s capacity throughout the year. Falcon 9 has become the world’s most frequently launched orbital rocket, with the booster reuse program now routine. SpaceX’s ability to reflew the same booster dozens of times has fundamentally changed spaceflight economics, reducing launch costs and enabling the company to deploy satellites at an accelerated pace. The 28-flight record on this particular booster demonstrates the durability of the design and SpaceX’s operational proficiency in managing a large fleet of reusable rockets. records.excerpt: SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket deployed 27 Starlink internet satellites from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California on Sunday morning. Skip to content SpaceX launches 27 Starlink satellites from California on Falcon 9 Published on 14 July 2026 at 9:08 am • Written by Chris Martin · read 15 times © SpaceX launches 27 Starlink satellites from California on Falcon 9 Post on Facebook Post on Flipboard Share on LinkedIn Post on Reddit Share on Telegram Share on X Send through Whatsapp SpaceX launched 27 Starlink satellites on a Falcon 9 rocket from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California last night, continuing the company’s rapid cadence of broadband internet deployments to low Earth orbit. The Starlink 15-14 mission lifted off at 6:28 p.m. PDT on Sunday, July 13, from Space Launch Complex 4 East at Vandenberg. The Falcon 9 first stage booster, designated B1093, completed its 15th flight after previously launching two Space Development Agency missions and 11 batches of Starlink satellites, according to Spaceflight Now . About eight minutes after liftoff, the booster landed on the droneship “Of Course I Still Love You” in the Pacific Ocean. This marked the 210th landing on that vessel and the 637th booster landing overall for SpaceX, demonstrating the company’s continued mastery of reusable rocket technology. The constellation now holds more than 10,700 operational Starlink satellites in orbit, providing global broadband coverage. SpaceX has deployed approximately 1,000 Starlink satellites so far in 2026, maintaining a launch cadence of roughly one mission every 2.5 days and adding about 10 satellites to the network daily. The Starlink 15-14 mission deployed V2 Mini variants, the optimized design SpaceX has standardized for rapid constellation expansion. Each satellite operates at approximately 550 kilometers altitude, communicating with ground gateways that connect the constellation to terrestrial internet infrastructure. records.title: New Zealand investors among those losing money in SpaceX price slump
records.excerpt: New Zealand investors among those losing money in SpaceX price slump | RNZ Skip to main content 16 July 2026, 11:16am New Zealand investors among those losing money in SpaceX price slump Susan Edmunds Caption: Elon Musk became the world's first trillionaire after SpaceX went public on 12 June 2026. Photo credit: NurPhoto via AFP SpaceX's share price slump is a reminder to New Zealand investors of the hype that can circle a new listing, commentators say. The price of shares has fallen from a peak of more than US$200 to around US$135 and has at times dipped below that IPO price . The drop has cut the company's value by nearly US$1 trillion, and cost founder Elon Musk his US trillionaire status. Many New Zealanders will have been affected by the share price movements - Sharesies said SpaceX had generated very strong interest with its IPO and trading in the shares since. "We were pleased with the allocation that we were able to get for our investors who applied," co-chief executive Leighton Roberts said mid last month. "It has also been a popular choice over the last couple of days on the secondary market." Who gets all your stuff when you die? No Stupid Questions with Susan Edmunds AUT professor of finance Aaron Gilbert said SpaceX was a good example of a company that tended to attract a lot of hype. "It has an exciting story, enormous potential, and a wide divergence in opinion, with many investors extremely optimistic about its future. Add to that the fact that only around 5 percent of the company's shares are publicly traded, and it is relatively easy for those optimistic investors to have a strong influence on the initial share price. Over time, however, the shareholder base broadens and investors with more cautious views begin to have a greater influence on pricing, so it is not unusual to see some of that initial enthusiasm unwind." He said share prices ultimately reflected information and expectations about the future. "At around $200 per share, investors needed a great deal of SpaceX's future potential to become reality-Starship to be commercially successful, Starlink to become the dominant global satellite internet platform, and newer ventures such as floating AI data centres to generate substantial profits. "At the same time, the economic backdrop is becoming less favourable, with the possibility of higher interest rates increasing investors' required returns. Because so much of SpaceX's value depends on cash flows that are many years into the future, even relatively small changes in expectations about growth, profitability or interest rates can have a large impact on today's share price. "The result is that SpaceX is likely to remain a volatile investment. Small pieces of positive or negative news can produce outsized share price movements because investors are continually reassessing a business whose value depends much more on what it might become than on what it earns today. It is also worth remembering that, even after the recent pullback, SpaceX is not obviously a cheap stock. Investors make money by buying businesses for less than they are ultimately worth, and companies that already trade on very high valuation multiples - whether measured by price-to-sales or other metrics-leave much less room for disappointment." The Nasdaq MarketSite after SpaceX range the opening bell to launch SpaceX's initial public offering in New York on 12 June 2026. AFP Forsyth Barr senior equities analyst Aaron Ibbotson said AI "hype" in general had weakened. "SpaceX is one of those proper FOMO stocks, and if there is no missing out, then the fear subsides. Proper momentum stock. It goes up because it goes up and then down because it goes down. Stocks with limited connection to fundamentals move on sentiment." Kernel founder Dean Anderson said it was common to see excitement about IPOs that then waned. "I think it's a common trait of a lot of IPOs… where the IPO process involves suspense and the build-up to the moment and there's a lot of sales activity going on. We saw that with SpaceX, where everybody wanted a piece of this thing. There was a lot of curiosity around is it going to be included in the indices? What does that mean? And there was a relatively small portion of capital being raised so the expectation was that there's a bit of a fight over who's going to get a share of that small amount of equity that becomes available." He said there had been concerns about the "fairly lofty" valuation that was based on long-term, ambitious assumptions for the company. "It doesn't mean it won't achieve them over the long term but a lot of that is already baked into the assumption at the price that it came to market." Anderson said it was so easy for everyday investors to buy shares in the US market now that it drove prices up. "As that initial buying activity eases, people have effectively done their shopping and what we're seeing is the price starting to come back down." He said it was now included in the indices that were going to pick it up straight away and the S&P would not add it for 12 months or more, so that would not provide additional buying support for a while. "The next big moment is going to be when it releases its first set of quarterly reports. For now there's no new information available. People are going to be having a close eye on how well is Starlink going? What does the pathway look like for X? How much is being spent on AI infrastructure? I think we need to wait and see until that next set of reporting comes through in terms of is it on track or maybe it's got some headwinds." He said it would also be interesting to look back in 12 or 18 months' time to see whether it was worthwhile holding SpaceX early or whether holding off proved the better plan. records.title: CPI鈍化でFRBの7月利上げ観測が大幅後退｜暗号資産市場の動向
records.excerpt: 2026年7月14日（火）、FRBの7月29日会合での利上げ確率は約15%まで低下し、1週間前の約40%から急落しました。要因は、主要指標すべてで市場予想より弱かった6月のCPI（消費者物価指数）です。これにより、特に懸念されていた「原油高下での利上げ」というシナリオが現実味を失いました。 この動きが特異なのは、2026年を通じて多くの議論が「利下げの回数」に集中していたのに対し、今回は「利上げ」が焦点だったためです。FRB議長のケビン・ウォーシュ氏率いる委員会は、7月8日に米国とイランの停戦が崩壊し、原油価格が上昇したことで、インフレ高進への警戒から利上げの可能性を検討していました。しかし、CPIが予想を下回ったことでリスク資産市場は一時的な安心感を得ました。 2026年7月15日時点のFRB動向要約： 7月29日利上げ確率： 約15%（1週間前は約40%） 7月29日据え置き確率： 約70% 2026年内の利下げ： 予想市場では約76%が「ゼロ回」と見積もり 6月CPI： 前月比-0.4%、前年同月比3.5%（5月は4.2%） コアCPI： 前月比0.0%、前年比2.6%（2月以来の低水準） リスク資産の反応： BTC $64,466（+3.18%）、ETH $1,865（+4.73%）、XRP $1.099、SOL $77.15 この上昇は事実ですが、背景は見出しより限定的です。今朝発表の指標が新たな試金石となります。以下、FRBの反応の変化が暗号資産ポジションにどう影響するか、今後のリスク要因もまとめます。 PhemexでBTCを取引する 7月利上げ観測が一晩で40%から15%に低下した理由 今回の動向を理解するには、FRBのスタンスを知る必要があります。週初時点でフェッドファンド先物は7月29日の利上げ確率を約40%と見積もっており、今サイクル初の利上げとなる見込みもありました。原動力は原油です。7月8日に停戦が崩れるとブレント原油が急騰し、FRBの利上げ観測が強まりました。 しかし、 6月のCPI 発表でこの議論は覆されました。総合インフレ率は前月比-0.4%と2020年4月以来の大幅下落、前年比でも3.5%と5月の4.2%から鈍化しました。エネルギー指数が5.7%低下したことが大きな要因です。さらに委員会が重視するコアインフレも前月比0.0%、前年比2.6%と2月以来の低水準でした。 インフレが6年ぶりのペースで鈍化する中で利上げは難しく、市場は数時間で織り込み直し、7月29日利上げ確率は約15%に下落しました。リスク資産に重くのしかかっていた「最悪ケース」の根拠が消えた形です。 これは「利上げ後退」であって「利下げ期待」ではない理由 この部分が誤解されやすく、間違うと次の指標で過度なリスクを取る原因になります。弱いCPIは「利下げ局面」の始まりではなく「最悪シナリオの回避」を意味します。両者は全く異なり、市場価格にも明確に反映されています。 7月29日の「据え置き」確率は約70%と高く、年内全体を見ても利下げの予想は約76%が「ゼロ回」となっています。従って「流動性相場再開」と捉えるのは誤りで、「リスク資産の下値不安が後退した」と読み取るのが妥当です。フェッドファンド先物から会合別確率を算出する CME FedWatch ツール で推移を確認できます。 この違いはポジションサイズにも直結します。「利上げ見送り」は一時的な反発を支える一方、「利下げ開始」なら積極的な買い増しも合理的です。現状でレバレッジを強めるのは、市場が約1/4しか織り込んでいないシナリオに賭けることになります。"リスク資産に下値ができた"程度の認識が現実的です。 割引率変動が暗号資産に与えた影響 このメカニズムは、なぜ一部保有資産が他より大きく動いたのかを説明します。暗号資産は「長期・高ベータ」型のリスク資産です。2026年の最大マクロ要因はオンチェーン動向よりも金利期待の方向性です。 金利期待が上昇すれば、将来価値を割り引くレートも上昇し、リスクの高い資産ほど厳しい修正を受けます。逆に上昇が止まると、同じ資産が一番大きな反発を見せやすくなります。 実際、 ビットコイン は64,000ドル台を回復し、ETHも4.73%上昇。高ベータの主要銘柄も同様に反発しました。この動きは暗号資産だけでなく、NvidiaなどAI半導体関連にも波及しました。これらは「将来収益への長期投資」として割引率で動きます。 トレーダー目線では、これは「機械的な再評価」であって「市場心理の好転」ではありません。突然暗号資産への好感度が高まったわけでなく、バリュエーション計算の分母（割引率）が小さくなったので、将来価値の大きい資産が先に反応したのです。実需筋の資金流入状況は、日次の ビットコインETFフロー などがより客観的な指標となります。 PhemexでBTCを取引する 本日のPPI（卸売物価指数）が真の試金石 この安心感には「期限」が存在し、それは今朝のPPI（卸売物価指数）発表です。6月PPIは7月15日（水）8:30am（米東部）に発表予定で、総合は前月比-0.1%が市場予想です。注目は内訳であり、コアPPIはやや強含みが予想されています。卸売物価はFRBが政策決定の際に重視するPCEデフレーターに直結するため、重要度はCPI以上です。 PPIがCPIの安心感を打ち消す可能性がある理由はここにあります。FRBはCPIではなく コアPCE に注目しており、PCEの主要構成要素、特に医療や金融サービスはPPIのデータを参照しています。仮に総合が穏やかでもコアが強ければ、デフレ期待はやや後退し、再び利上げ議論に火が付きかねません。公式発表は BLS PPIページ で確認できます。 ポジショニング観点では、今日の動きはチャートだけでは見えない「二択性」を持ちます。無難なPPIなら「利上げ観測後退」が強化され、安心感がFOMCカレンダーまで続く余地があります。一方、コアが強ければCPIで消えたはずの議論が再燃し、高ベータ資産が一番先に値を戻すリスクもあります。 CPIデータで生じたエネルギー要因の変化 もうひとつ、安心感を慎重に扱うべき理由はCPIの内訳にあります。6月の鈍化はエネルギー指数の-5.7%寄与が大きく、つまり「エネルギー安頼み」の側面が強かったのです。 しかしこの要因はCPI発表後に反転し、7月14日にはブレント原油が86ドル台に上昇しています。従って、CPIの好結果は中東情勢の安定によるものではなく、むしろ「エネルギー高でも市場は割引率再評価で反発した」という構図です。 実務的には、「今月最も効いた下押し要因が来月は逆風に転じやすい」点に注意が必要です。これは安心感を否定するものではありませんが、インフレリスク全体が消えたわけではなく、「一時的リスクリプライシング」と捉えるのが現実的です。 よくある質問 FRBは2026年7月に利上げしますか？ おそらくしません。CPIが弱かったことで、フェッドファンド先物は7月29日の利上げ確率を約15%と織り込み、据え置きが最有力（約70%）となっています。リスクは「強気据え置き」ですが、実際の利上げは考えにくくなっています。 CPIが弱いとFRBはすぐ利下げしますか？ いいえ。両者を混同するのがよくある誤解です。CPIは利上げリスクを後退させましたが、利下げ予想を前倒ししたわけではありません。予想市場でも2026年内の利下げ（ゼロ回）が76%と見積もられています。 FRBの利上げがビットコイン・暗号資産に与える影響は？ 暗号資産は「長期・高ベータ」型のリスク資産で、将来価値を割り引く金利に非常に敏感です。金利期待が上昇すれば価格は下落し、利上げ観測が後退すれば反発しやすくなります。 今週のPPI（卸売物価指数）が暗号資産に重要な理由は？ PPIは卸売インフレを測り、FRBが重視するコアPCEに直結しています。7月15日のPPIコアが強ければ、CPIで和らいだ利上げ観測が再燃し、リスク資産に即時の下押し圧力となる可能性があります。 まとめ 7月29日のベースケースは「据え置き」で、市場が「利上げリスクの後退」を織り込んだ形です。この違いがポジショニングのポイントとなります。現状は「リスク資産の下値が固まった」状態であり、利下げ開始とはみなされていません。今朝発表のPPIコア次第では再び利上げ議論が浮上する可能性があり、その後は7月29日の決定とウォーシュ議長の指針、ブレント原油動向にも注目です。安心感は一時的ですが、全面的なリスク解消とは言えません。 PhemexでBTCを取引する 本記事は情報提供のみを目的としており、投資助言を行うものではありません。暗号資産取引には大きなリスクが伴います。投資判断はご自身で調査の上、慎重に行ってください。

records.title: Cooler CPI, Hotter Risk Appetite: Data Slams Door on July Fed Rate Hike
records.excerpt: June's CPI surprises to the downside, giving the Fed room to keep rates steady and boosting stocks. June’s cooler‑than‑expected Consumer Price Index print gave the Federal Reserve breathing room to hold rates steady this month, sending U.S. stocks modestly higher as traders slashed the odds of a near‑term hike. The SPY is moving higher. See the chart and price action here. The S&P 500 edged up, the Nasdaq 100 climbed about 0.7%, and the Dow pared earlier losses to turn green while growth and rate‑sensitive names caught a bid on the benign inflation surprise. CPI Print Details Headline CPI fell 0.4% month‑over‑month in June, pulling the annual inflation rate down to 3.5%. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, was flat at zero percent on the month, leaving the year‑over‑year rate around 2.6% and marking the coolest core print since 2021, according to Trading Economics. The cooling was driven largely by lower gasoline prices and easing shelter costs, helping offset the impact of another rally in energy as the U.S. and Iran maintained strikes against each other. Read Also: Squeeze Watch: 10 Stocks Bears Love to Hate Most Right Now Expert Voices Liz Thomas, chief market strategist at SoFi, highlighted how surprising the core result was versus consensus. "June core CPI came in flat (-0.03%) vs the est of +0.2% m/m," she wrote, noting that "the drivers were relatively broad-based (e.g. shelter, medical services, etc). Odds of a July rate hike fell from 40% to 14% in response." June core CPI came in flat (-0.03%) vs the est of +0.2% m/m. That's the lowest m/m print since May 2020, and the drivers were relatively broad-based (e.g. shelter, medical services, etc). Odds of a July rate hike fell from 40% to 14% in response. pic.twitter.com/f4cK81MX45— Liz Thomas (@LizThomasStrat) July 14, 2026 Investors welcomed the broad‑based relief in the report as a sign that inflation momentum is finally slowing rather than simply rotating across categories. Jamie Cox, managing partner at Harris Financial Group, said the data undercuts fears that the spring inflation bump was the start of a new uptrend. "If you were looking for runaway inflation in this report, you didn't get it," he said. "It's pretty clear any recent rise in inflation was related to energy prices and wouldn't be long-lasting." Jeffrey Roach, chief economist at LPL Financial in Charlotte, pointed to service categories as a potential turning point. "Prices within transportation services and medical care services declined in June, setting up what could be a decelerating trend in consumer inflation. Investors cheered the report," he said. Roach noted "core inflation decelerated to 2.59% year over year, the lowest since February and should further in Q3 and Q4 as durable goods prices improve," while warning "the big risk is still geopolitical" and an improvement in supply chains by Labor Day would be key to a more decisive inflation downtrend. Bill Adams, chief U.S. economist at Fifth Third, framed the release as a critical but incomplete win. "The June CPI report was much better than expected, with a drop in headline prices and core inflation flat," he said. "June CPI much cooler than expected, likely justifying a Fed hold at the July decision; more good inflation news needed to stay the Fed's hand through year-end." Adams added that "on top of lower gasoline, June saw broad-based declines in core goods prices as businesses discounted to keep consumers spending," even as "longer-run inflationary pressures persist from labor shortages in industries with high shares of immigrant workers (nursing care, home health care, etc.) and climate change (beef prices). Even so, these goods and services comprise relatively small shares of the CPI basket." Read Also: Evercore’s Beat‑and‑Raise 4: Why Nvidia, Alphabet, Netflix and Booking May Finally Catch a Bid Eyes on the Fed For policymakers, Adams argued, the report is enough to pause but not to declare victory. "For the Fed, the better-than-expected June CPI report likely can justify refraining from a hike at the meeting late this month," he said. "The Fed will need to see more good news on inflation to hold off on interest rate hikes in the rest of the year. June’s CPI report is a big step in the right direction, but more is needed." Traders are treating the June CPI as a pivotal print that slams the door on a July move, but keeps the second half of 2026 in play. With core inflation near post‑2020 lows, equities have room to extend gains, but the combination of geopolitical energy risk and stubborn pockets of service inflation means every subsequent CPI release will be a live event for the Fed’s next move. Markets React SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE:SPY), which tracks the broad S&P 500 large-cap benchmark, was higher on the day, reflecting the index’s steady grind up after the soft CPI print. Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ), the Nasdaq 100 tracker, outperformed with a stronger gain as traders rotated into mega-cap tech and growth on cooling core inflation. SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (NYSE:DIA), which mirrors the price action of the 30‑stock Dow Jones Industrial Average, was roughly flat, underscoring the more muted reaction in blue-chip cyclicals. records.title: Bitcoin Rallies to $65,000 as Cooling CPI Cuts July Fed Hike Odds
records.excerpt: Table of Contents Bitcoin climbed to $65,950 on Wednesday morning Asia time, up 4% from the prior day, as cooling inflation data reduced expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike at the central bank's July meeting. Ethereum followed, rising 5% to $1,873, while broader equity markets also showed strength: the S&P 500 (SPY) rose 0.36% to $751.83, and the Nasdaq (QQQ) gained 1.12% to $719.71 during Tuesday's session. The move reflects a classic risk-on reversal. Investors had bet on a July rate hike after recent inflation readings remained sticky. Fresh data suggesting inflation is cooling shifted those bets sharply, with fed futures now pricing a near-zero probability of a hike at the next meeting. That relief translated immediately into crypto assets, which had endured selling pressure in the days before the release. The VIX, a measure of equity volatility, fell 3.85% on the news, signaling reduced anxiety across broader markets. Bitcoin and altcoins tend to underperform when volatility spikes and risk appetite declines. The inverse is true when volatility contracts and equity traders see reduced downside risk. For context, Bitcoin had come under pressure throughout the past week as traders gamed the probability of a July hike. The asset has historically struggled when real interest rates rise – which a Fed hike would signal – because higher rates reduce the appeal of non-yielding assets like Bitcoin. With that risk now materially lower, traders repositioned back into crypto. The strength in Ethereum outpaced Bitcoin, a sign that traders are rotating into risk assets with more leverage to economic growth and technology adoption. ETH had underperformed Bitcoin during the period of macro uncertainty. The 5% move in a single day suggests traders had been crowded into bearish bets, and the inflation news forced rapid repositioning. What happens next depends on whether the Fed actually skips July and when the central bank begins cutting rates. Markets are now fully priced for cuts by September. If inflation remains contained and the Fed confirms that expectation, crypto assets could continue to benefit from the tailwind of falling real interest rates. ➢ Stay ahead of the curve.
